ruleName: Summit & Pine outdoor-gear product page (Trail Runner GTX): color swatches show the color name in a hover bubble that has no focus path (swatch:hover .hover-name, no :focus equivalent) — superficially the same failure. But the color name is already printed as a persistent visible <span> under each swatch AND is each radio's accessible name (aria-label='Pine' etc.). The hover bubble is aria-hidden and purely redundant, so the missing focus path deprives no one of additional perceivable content. Redundancy decoy → PASS.

SaaS analytics dashboard: a '?' badge on a conversion KPI opens a definition popover that covers the device-breakdown list. The popover is hoverable and persistent, but its only dismiss affordance is a close '×' button positioned INSIDE the popover, reachable only by Tab-ing focus off the trigger and into the additional content. No Escape handler and no toggle-on-trigger.

RTL (Arabic) API-reference docs: a dotted-underline glossary term 'cursor' shows a hover-only tooltip on a non-focusable span that covers the curl example block. A document-level Escape handler exists but its dismiss branch is gated on document.activeElement being a text input (copied from the filter box's clear-on-Esc behavior); while hovering the term nothing is focused, so the guard is false and Escape is inert.

Long-form policy article: an inline glossary-term tooltip (Emissions Trading System) opens downward on hover/focus with no Esc dismiss, landing on the first ~3 lines of the next body paragraph. Method 2 absent, so Method 1 is the only path — and it obscures meaningful body text.

Banco Aurora high-yield savings page: a circular info 'i' icon next to '4.35% APY' reveals a hover-only popup disclosing a material tiered-rate caveat (4.35% only up to $250,000; above that 0.50%) found nowhere else on the page. The trigger is a non-focusable <span> with only mouseover/mouseout handlers, so keyboard, switch, and magnifier users never see the cap.

Loom Analytics campaign dashboard: the Conversions KPI card has a focusable '?' <button> whose tooltip explains a non-obvious 7-day post-click attribution model (why the number is lower than the ad platform's 28-day count). The button is a real tab stop with aria-label, aria-describedby, and a visible focus ring, but the JS binds the reveal only to mouseover/mouseout and never to focus/focusin, so focus produces no tooltip.

The Tidewater Review economics article: FOMC and bps are plain abbr title= (native, UA-controlled, out of scope / PASS), while GDP looks identical (same dotted underline) but is an abbr.gloss wrapping a span.bub author tooltip that JS reveals on hover/focus. The author bubble is pointer-events:none with no Escape handler. Two visually identical abbreviations, different owners — only the GDP one is governed by 1.4.13, and it fails; the reviewer must attribute each bubble element-by-element.

Online-banking transfer-limit screen: a round 'i' info button shows a tooltip on hover AND keyboard focus that overlaps the help paragraph and the Continue button. The tooltip is keyboard-reachable (meets 2.1.1) but there is NO Escape handler, no documented shortcut, and activating the trigger does not toggle it off — the only way to clear the obscuring content is to move focus/pointer off the trigger.

Patient-portal medication list: an 'interactions' pill on Warfarin opens a drug-interaction warning box that covers the dosage text. An Escape handler exists but is bound to the trigger button; the trigger's own click handler calls this.blur(), moving focus to document.body, so the keydown never reaches the handler and Escape is inert while the box obscures the dose.

Community forum thread: a GitHub/Twitter-style profile "hover card" appears when hovering a username. It is rendered into a detached portal layer (#hovercard-layer, sibling of the content) positioned 12px below the username. Show is delayed 180ms (hover-intent); hide is immediate on the username's mouseleave; the card has no mouseenter of its own. Moving the pointer down to the card crosses the 12px transparent gap, fires mouseleave, and the card vanishes instantly.

PASSING counter-fixture. Higher-ed LMS reading with a '[1]' footnote reference that opens a citation popup on hover AND keyboard focus, deliberately overlapping the paragraph below (so Method 1 is not relied on). A document-level Escape handler hides the popup while focus REMAINS on the '[1]' button, and activating the trigger also toggles it closed — both SCR39-allowed dismissals.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-revealed tooltip content remains visible indefinitely while the trigger is hovered or focused without automatically dismissing on a timer.
The additional hover content remains visible and persistent while the trigger is hovered without withdrawing itself on a timer.

ruleName: SaaS billing page: a "?" help button beside "Seat overage" shows a custom tooltip positioned 30px BELOW the trigger, separated by a transparent .gap spacer (pointer-events:none). Show/hide is bound only to the trigger button's mouseover/mouseout; the tooltip has no hover handler and is not a descendant of the trigger. Moving the pointer down to read the tooltip crosses the gap, fires mouseout, and the tooltip vanishes before the pointer reaches it.

Pharmacy prescription page: a glossary term <dfn> ("contraindication") shows a definition pop-up that DIRECTLY overlaps/adjoins the term (top:-2px, no gap) — visually the passing arrangement the Understanding describes. But the pop-up carries pointer-events:none and reveal is keyed only to the term's :hover, so moving the pointer onto the pop-up means the cursor is no longer counted as over the term, :hover collapses, and the content vanishes. Adjacency is present but the content is not actually hoverable.

The Tideline Review newsletter-signup promo (Privy/Mailchimp-style) appears over a dark scrim as a centered card. It looks modal and the developer moved initial focus into the email field, but there is NO focus trap and the background was never made inert/aria-hidden. Tabbing forward from the email field walks past Subscribe onto the article's 'Search the archive' input and button, hidden under the scrim; Shift+Tab leaks too.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus sequence traverses the header search controls and the subscription form in a logical, unbroken order.

ruleName: LMS course home (BIO 210): a wide main course-content column (module links + Start quiz) on the left and a narrow, UNRELATED site-wide 'Annual Fund' donation widget on the right. The donation aside is DOM-first but flex order paints it right. No tabindex, no JS. Verified tab order: donation amount, Donate now, THEN the course links/quiz — right column focuses first, but the columns are independent.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus sequence traverses the independent sidebar promo in its entirety before systematically traversing the main coursework content.

ruleName: E-commerce garden-seed product page with pill-badge triggers; on hover/focus each reveals a role=tooltip with multi-sentence guidance. The auto-dismiss is implemented entirely in CSS — a @keyframes peekThenVanish animation with animation-fill-mode:forwards drives the popup to opacity:0 after ~3.5s while the badge is still hovered/focused; there is NO setTimeout/setInterval anywhere. Verified: opacity 1 at 0s -> opacity 0 at 4s while still hovering.

Ledgerline invoicing toolbar: every button (Save/Export/Send/Duplicate) carries only a native title= attribute (e.g. title='Save your work'). There is zero JavaScript and no author popup DOM, so the hover bubble is rendered entirely by the user agent. This is the out-of-scope boundary anchor: visually similar to the author-built failing cases, but UA-controlled and therefore inapplicable / PASS by exclusion.

Northbridge Bank 'Confirm transfer' modal (dim backdrop + centered card). A hand-rolled focus trap wraps only the FORWARD direction; the Shift+Tab branch was never written. Forward Tab is perfectly trapped, but Shift+Tab from the first control (the amount field) falls through to the browser default and lands on the page header's 'Log out' link behind the non-inert backdrop.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus escapes the open modal dialog when navigating backward, reaching background navigation links.
The recorded focus sequence follows a logical top-to-bottom and left-to-right order through the form controls and action buttons.

ruleName: Real-estate listing: the entire large Walk Score hero tile is the hover/focus trigger; its explainer popover is pushed away into the next column to avoid the trigger, but lands on the Monthly cost estimate breakdown. No Esc dismiss. Tests the large-trigger 'Method 2 only' nuance.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover tooltip obscures adjacent page content and cannot be dismissed with the Escape key or any other in-place mechanism.
The hover-revealed tooltip remains visible when moving the pointer onto it.
The hover-triggered tooltip persists for as long as the trigger remains hovered and does not self-withdraw on a timer.

ruleName: Healthcare new-patient intake form: a 'What's this?' help popover on the Insurance Member ID field opens down-right with no Esc dismiss and overlaps the next field's required asterisk + label (Patient date of birth) and the input being filled.

Bakery (Birchwood Bakehouse) footer with a flex row of five social-media links. DOM order is Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest, YouTube; CSS `order` paints them Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok, Pinterest. No tabindex, no JS. Verified tab order (DOM) differs from visual left-to-right order, but the links are an orderless set.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus moves among a collection of orderless social media peer links where no meaningful sequence or dependency exists.

ruleName: City government primary nav: a 'Residents & Services' submenu opens on hover and on activation/focus of its toggle and covers the page banner and intro text. It carries aria-haspopup/aria-expanded/aria-controls, but the only way it closes is a document-level click outside the menu (pointer only) — no Escape handler and activating the toggle only re-opens it, so keyboard/magnifier users cannot dismiss the obscuring panel without moving focus away.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No additional content or tooltip is triggered on hover or focus of the Government navigation link.
No additional content is revealed upon hovering over the Government navigation link.
The navigation item does not trigger any additional content on hover or focus, exhibiting no self-withdrawing content barrier under WCAG 1.4.13.
No additional content or overlay is revealed when hovering or focusing the Business navigation link.
Hovering over the Business navigation item does not reveal any additional content or popup, so no hoverability barrier exists under WCAG 1.4.13.
The element does not trigger any additional content on hover or focus, so no self-withdrawal barrier exists under WCAG 1.4.13.

ruleName: Meridian Bank wire-transfer form: focusing the high-risk Amount field opens a modal security step-up dialog (role='dialog' aria-modal='true') that dims the page, moves keyboard focus to its confirm button, traps Tab, and is dismissed via Escape/Cancel. Superficially this is content appearing on focus (the 1.4.13 trigger pattern), but modal dialogs are explicitly out of scope — the correct disposition is NOT-APPLICABLE to 1.4.13 (evaluate under 3.2.1 On Focus). This is the N/A modal carve-out anchor.

Government DMV registration-renewal wizard: focus-triggered help bubbles (role=tooltip) under the Plate and VIN fields. A single global setInterval(...,5000) clears any visible bubble every 5 seconds, so the VIN help vanishes while the field still has focus and the user is mid-task. Verified: visible on focus -> display:none at 6s while document.activeElement is still #vin.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus-revealed tooltip remains visible while the input retains focus and does not withdraw itself on a timer.

ruleName: Government parking-permit form: a "?" help tooltip beside the "Parking zone" select, built correctly as the PASS anchor on the same component family. Trigger and tooltip share one wrapper (.help) whose box encloses both; reveal is keyed to the wrapper's mouseenter/mouseleave and focus-within. The tooltip is adjacent/overlapping (4px overlap, no gap), has pointer-events:auto and its own mouseenter, a 120ms hide delay tolerates the sub-element transition, and Esc dismisses it. A continuous pointer path from button to tooltip keeps the content visible.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-triggered help tooltip remains persistently visible while the trigger is held and does not disappear on an automatic timer.
The hover-revealed tooltip remains persistently visible while the trigger is held and does not disappear on a timer.

ruleName: ATS job application (Talentforge) Background step, single-column layout with two stacked sections — Education (Highest degree, School/university, Graduation year) wholly above Work experience (Most recent job title, Most recent company, Years in role). The DOM interleaves the two sections row-by-row (education-degree, work-title, education-school, work-company, ...) and CSS grid pins each field into its section block, so with no tabindex keyboard focus jumps ~300px down to Work and back up to Education on alternate Tabs while a sighted user sees two clean stacked blocks.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order alternates back and forth between inputs in the Education section and inputs in the Work Experience section instead of completing either section sequentially.

ruleName: RTL Arabic (lang=ar, dir=rtl) two-attendee conference registration (مؤتمر الابتكار التقني) with two grouped, headed cards — الحاضر الأول (Attendee 1, on the right per RTL) and الحاضر الثاني (Attendee 2, on the left) — each with full name, email, job title, dietary preference. The DOM interleaves the two attendees field-by-field, so with no tabindex keyboard focus alternates between the right (Attendee 1) and left (Attendee 2) cards on every Tab.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order repeatedly alternates between the input fields of the two separate attendee cards instead of completing one attendee's form before moving to the next.

ruleName: Municipal parking-permit page (City of Aldergrove): a left-hand 'Parking services' nav and a wide application form on the right. The nav is authored AFTER <main> in the DOM and CSS Grid (grid-template-areas) paints it left. No tabindex, no JS. Verified tab order reaches the main form (plate, zone, email, submit) FIRST, then the side-nav links — the Understanding's own passing source-order technique.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order traverses the complete main application form followed by the side navigation, preserving meaning and task operability.

ruleName: Calverton DMV 'Confirm renewal & payment' modal. The developer used the modern recommended technique — set the page wrapper's inert=true and rely on inert (no JS trap) to contain focus. But a OneTrust-style cookie-consent banner was injected by the tag manager as a direct child of <body>, OUTSIDE the inerted #page wrapper, so its 'Accept all cookies' / 'Manage' buttons stay focusable. Tab off the dialog's last control and Shift+Tab off its first control both land on the cookie buttons.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Keyboard focus escapes the open modal dialog to background controls in the cookie banner.
The focus sequence follows a logical and predictable order across the interactive controls.

ruleName: Al-Nakheel Clinic (Arabic, lang=ar dir=rtl) 'Confirm appointment' modal. The developer hand-rolled the dialog (no native <dialog>) but did containment correctly: on open they set the background wrapper inert AND aria-hidden=true, and installed a keydown handler that wraps BOTH directions (Tab on last -> first, Shift+Tab on first -> last). In RTL the visual left/right is mirrored but Tab semantics are unchanged. Focus never escapes the modal in either direction. PASS boundary that directly contrasts case-01.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Keyboard focus remains strictly contained within the open modal dialog across all navigation stops.
The focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom and right-to-left sequence through the dialog form fields and action buttons.

ruleName: RTL Arabic e-commerce product page: a size-guide tooltip authored with physical left:0 does not mirror under dir=rtl and opens on top of its own trigger button, covering the label 'دليل المقاسات'. No Esc dismiss. Obscures the trigger itself — FAIL.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The captured state-after frame is identical to state-before, so the revealed hover or focus content cannot be visually evaluated for dismissability.
The hover-triggered tooltip disappears when the pointer moves toward it.
The additional content revealed on hover or focus persists and does not dismiss itself while the trigger remains active.

ruleName: Aurora Transit trip planner: each leg has a round service-note icon where the author sets title='' to suppress the native tooltip, then paints an identical gray bubble with a pure-CSS ::after { content: attr(data-hint) } (no JavaScript). The bubble appears only while the 22px icon itself is :hovered; a ::after pseudo-element cannot receive the pointer and there is no Escape affordance. Indistinguishable from a native tooltip, but author CSS owns it, so 1.4.13 applies and it fails.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The custom tooltip appears in empty space above the trigger without obscuring or replacing any other content, meeting the obscuring exemption under WCAG 1.4.13.
The hover-revealed tooltip is separated from its trigger icon by a physical gap with no hoverable bridge, preventing the pointer from moving over the content without dismissing it.
The hover/focus-triggered hint content remains visible for the entire duration the trigger is held and does not withdraw itself on a timer.
The hover/focus tooltip obscures underlying content and cannot be dismissed in place.
The hover-revealed tooltip is separated from its trigger by a gap and rendered via CSS pseudo-content, making it impossible to move the pointer onto the additional content without dismissing it.
The hover/focus hint does not self-withdraw on a timer while the trigger remains hovered or focused.
The custom hover tooltip obscures adjacent content and cannot be dismissed without moving pointer or focus.
The hover-triggered tooltip cannot be hovered because it floats above the trigger with a physical gap and is rendered via a CSS pseudo-element.
The hover/focus tooltip remains persistent while the trigger is held and does not automatically withdraw on a timer.

ruleName: Nonprofit contact form (Riverbend Animal Rescue) with a contact-message column (Name, Email, Message) on the left and a 'How did you hear about us?' checkbox group (Instagram, From a friend, Web search, Event or flyer) on the right. The checkbox divs are spliced between the contact fields in DOM source order, so with no tabindex the tab sequence is Name -> Instagram -> Email -> From a friend -> Message -> Web search -> Event -> Send — the Understanding document's own failing example recast as a contact form.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order alternates between fields in the contact form and individual checkboxes in the survey section, disrupting the logical flow and meaning of both form sections.

ruleName: Round-trip flight search (SkyHop) with two vertically stacked, headed panels — Outbound flight (From, To, Depart date, Passengers) above Return flight (From, To, Return date, Cabin). The DOM emits the eight fields in alternating legs (outbound-From, return-From, outbound-To, return-To, ...) and CSS grid routes each field back into its panel, so with no tabindex keyboard focus bounces between the outbound and return legs on every Tab while a sighted user sees two clean stacked cards.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order repeatedly alternates between fields in the 'Outbound flight' section and the 'Return flight' section, disrupting the logical task flow.

ruleName: Joint loan application (Meridian Credit Union) with two side-by-side boxed sections — Applicant and Co-applicant — each with Full name, Date of birth, Annual income, Employer. Visually near-identical to the failing dual-section cases, but each section is a real fieldset containing its own fields in order, so the natural DOM order keeps each group whole: all four applicant fields are tabbed before any co-applicant field (the G59 passing pattern). PASS counter-example included so a judge cannot pass the failing cases by merely detecting 'two groups exist.'

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows a logical, whole-column traversal from the Applicant section to the Co-applicant section and finally to the submit button.

ruleName: Northwind Pharmacy refill queue: each status help icon shipped with a native title=, but a Bootstrap/jQuery-UI-style tooltip plugin strips the native title on load (removeAttribute('title')) and renders its own gray span.nwtip styled to mimic the native UA tooltip. The author bubble is pointer-events:none, toggled only on mouseenter/mouseleave of the 18px icon, with no Escape handler. Visually near-identical to the case-01 native tooltip, but author-owned, so 1.4.13 applies and it fails.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The custom hover tooltip cannot be dismissed with the Escape key or any other in-place dismissal mechanism while the pointer remains over the trigger.
The hover-revealed tooltip extinguishes when moving the pointer off the trigger toward the tooltip due to an unbridged gap.
The hover-triggered tooltip persists indefinitely while the trigger remains hovered or focused without self-withdrawing on a timer.
The hover tooltip occupies empty space and does not obscure or replace any other content, exempting it from the dismissable requirement under WCAG 1.4.13.
The hover-triggered tooltip is not hoverable because moving the pointer off the trigger toward the tooltip extinguishes it across a physical gap.
The hover-revealed tooltip remains visible persistently without automatically dismissing itself while the trigger remains hovered or focused.
The hover tooltip occupies empty space and does not obscure or replace any underlying content, qualifying for the 1.4.13 obscuring exemption.
The hover-revealed tooltip is not hoverable because a physical gap separates it from the trigger, causing the content to dismiss when moving the pointer toward it.
The hover-revealed tooltip remains visible persistently while the trigger is hovered without self-withdrawing on a timer.

ruleName: SaaS analytics cohort-retention grid with dotted-underline column-header terms; on hover/focus each reveals a role=tooltip definition. A scroll listener on the fixed-height, sticky-header scroller hides the popup the moment the user nudges the grid to read a lower row, although hover on the term is retained. Verified: visible before scroll -> hidden after scrollTop change.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-revealed tooltip remains persistent while the trigger is held and does not disappear on a timer.
The hover-revealed tooltip remains persistently visible while the trigger is hovered or focused without self-withdrawing.

ruleName: Hexagon Arena box-office 'Have a promo code?' jQuery-UI-style dialog. The developer moved initial focus in and restored it on close but never added a Tab wrap on the last control. Pressing Tab on the 'Apply code' button (the dialog's last control) follows DOM order to the page's first focusable element — a visually-hidden 'Skip to footer' skip-link — instead of cycling back to the first dialog control.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Keyboard focus escapes the open modal dialog to interactive elements behind the modal overlay.
The focus order follows a logical, predictable sequence through the navigation, footer, and form controls, preserving the meaning and operational flow of the content.

ruleName: E-commerce checkout (Northwind Outfitters) with two side-by-side boxed sections — Billing address and Shipping address — each visually holding Full name/Street/Apt/City/Postal in order. The whole form is one CSS grid; the DOM emits the two addresses interleaved line-by-line (billing-name, shipping-name, billing-street, shipping-street, ...), so with no tabindex the keyboard focus zig-zags between the billing and shipping cards on every Tab.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The keyboard focus order repeatedly alternates between fields in the Billing address and Shipping address sections rather than completing one section before moving to the next.

ruleName: Joint mortgage pre-approval form (Northgate Mutual) rendered as two titled columns — Primary applicant left, Co-applicant right — built with CSS Grid. The DOM interleaves the columns field-by-field and grid-column placement sorts each into its visual column. No tabindex, no JS. Verified tab order ping-pongs Primary-name, Co-applicant-name, Primary-DOB, Co-applicant-DOB, ... across two interdependent applicants.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order alternates row-by-row between the primary applicant and co-applicant columns instead of completing each section sequentially.

ruleName: Helios Energy kWh bar chart: each SVG rect bar has an SVG <title> child (UA-rendered native tooltip, e.g. 'February: 612 kWh', out of scope) AND an author .vtip floating overlay shown on hover with DIFFERENT, richer text ('Feb · 612 kWh · $84.10 · 18% below your 12-mo avg'). The overlay is pointer-events:none, repositions under the cursor via mousemove, and has no Escape handler. Two on-hover sources, two owners, two divergent texts — the reviewer must separate which content the SC governs (only the author overlay) and judge its behavior.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The additional hover content remains persistently visible while the trigger is hovered and does not dismiss itself on a timer.
The hover-revealed tooltip overlaps the trigger bar directly without any separating gap, satisfying the hoverable requirement of WCAG 1.4.13.
The hover-revealed content remains persistent and does not withdraw itself while the trigger remains hovered.
The hover-revealed additional content remains visible for as long as the trigger is hovered without self-withdrawing on a timer.
The hover-revealed tooltip disappears when the pointer moves off the trigger rect and onto the tooltip itself, failing the hoverability requirement.
The hover-revealed content persists continuously while the trigger remains hovered without self-withdrawing on an automatic timer.

ruleName: E-commerce category sidebar: hovering a top-level category ("Camp & Hike") reveals a CSS-only flyout submenu offset to the right (left:230px against a 210px row, leaving a ~20px transparent corridor). The flyout is a DOM child of the category but not geometrically contiguous; reaching lower submenu items requires a diagonal down-and-right path that exits both hot-zones, ending the :hover state and collapsing the flyout before the cursor arrives.

Single-page e-commerce checkout (Maple & Thread). A flex column whose 'Place order & pay' submit block is authored first in the DOM but pushed to the visual bottom with order:99. No tabindex, no JS. Verified tab order: T1 = the submit button (at y=1213, the visual bottom), then Quantity, Shipping, Payment — so Tab reaches the irreversible commit before any field.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The checkout submission button receives focus before all preceding quantity, shipping, and payment form fields.

ruleName: Arabic RTL airline seat-selection page: a held seat (C٢) shows, on hover/focus, a role=tooltip with the live remaining hold time (Arabic-Indic countdown). The popup stays visible the whole time the hold is valid and the seat is hovered; when the countdown reaches zero the hold genuinely expires (seat released, message now false) and the popup is removed because its information became invalid. Verified: visible through countdown ٠٠:٠٧ -> ٠٠:٠٤, removed only after real expiry, seat no longer held, pay button shows 'hold timed out'.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover/focus tooltip is dismissible in place using the Escape key without moving focus or pointer.
The hover-revealed tooltip remains visible when the pointer travels from the button trigger directly onto the tooltip content.
The hover-triggered tooltip persists and remains visible while the trigger button is held in hover state.

ruleName: Brightpath LMS 'Submit Lab Report 3' modal opened with native dialog.showModal() (UA-managed inert + containment). Inside, the formatting toolbar is an APG roving-tabindex group (one Tab stop, arrow-key navigation), so the FORWARD Tab order and the BACKWARD Shift+Tab order are intentionally NOT mirror images — yet focus never leaves the dialog and every control stays reachable and operable. PASS counter-example for the 'backward need not mirror forward' limb (TT 4.F step 2d).

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus is properly contained within the open modal dialog during keyboard navigation.
The focus order follows the logical and visual layout of the dialog controls sequentially from top to bottom.

ruleName: PASS boundary: a clinical 'add a patient allergy' form containing two focusable non-interactive elements placed where they do NOT impede operation — a role=status region (tabindex=-1) after the Save button that focus moves to on save, and a focusable end-of-form review summary placed AFTER all inputs and the submit button.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom sequence through the form fields and action controls, preserving meaning and operability.
The focusable summary section at the end of the form does not interrupt any input sequence or create an indistinguishable redundant stop.

ruleName: Telecom line-activation wizard, post-submit error state. Phone field is digits-only; the retained value is the all-digit string '12025550143'. The visible, aria-describedby-associated error reads 'Mobile number is invalid. Remove letters and parentheses from your phone number, then try again.' — describing a cause (letters/parentheses) that is factually absent from the value. The real defect (an 11-digit string for a 10-digit field) is never described.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message misidentifies the issue by instructing the user to remove letters and parentheses from an input value that contains only digits.

ruleName: Ticketing checkout where a decorative 'Payment details' text divider was made tabindex=0 (for a reveal-on-focus animation) and sits in source between the Card number input and the Expiry input, injecting a meaningless focus stop into the middle of the card-entry sequence.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom, left-to-right sequence through the checkout form fields and submit button, preserving meaning and operability.
An inoperable generic container is included in the focus sequence and interrupts data entry within the payment card form.

ruleName: Artisan pottery e-commerce product page where a focusable div[tabindex=0][role=button] wraps a real <button> 'Add to basket', so Tab stops on the wrapper then the button — the same control appears to receive focus twice (the exact div[tabindex=0]><button> shape pictured in the Understanding note).

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus sequence follows a logical order from the top navigation to the product selection and action controls.
A redundant focusable wrapper immediately precedes the button it encloses, causing the same control to be focused twice consecutively with identical name and geometry.

ruleName: SafeHarbor auto-insurance 'Quick Quote' wizard on one screen: numbered steps (1) About you, (2) Your vehicle, (3) Coverage & quote shown top-to-bottom with circular number badges. Panels are placed by CSS Grid grid-row but emitted in DOM order 3,1,2. No tabindex, no JS. Verified tab order: T1 = Step 3 coverage radio, T2 = 'Get my quote', then jumps up to Step 1 name/age/zip, then Step 2.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Keyboard focus starts at step 3 ('Coverage & quote') and its submit button before jumping back to step 1 ('About you') and step 2 ('Your vehicle'), breaking the multi-step form's logical sequence.

ruleName: Cedar Valley Health patient portal A1C trend chart: five hemoglobin A1C results are drawn as absolutely-positioned <div> markers; hovering reveals a popup with the exact value, date, and the provider's per-result clinical note (e.g. dose increased to 1000mg, recheck in 3 months). Those values and notes appear only in the hover popups (no data-table fallback). Markers are non-focusable <div>s with mouseenter/mouseleave-only popups, so keyboard users can read none of the data.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover/focus tooltip obscures underlying price and feature content and cannot be dismissed with Escape or any other in-place mechanism without moving focus or the pointer.
The hover-revealed tooltip disappears when moving the pointer from the trigger button toward the tooltip content.
Additional content revealed on hover and focus remains persistent and does not withdraw itself while the trigger is held.

ruleName: News/editorial site (The Meridian) full-screen search overlay opened from the masthead. On open it sets aria-hidden=false and moves focus into the search input; on Escape/Close it re-applies aria-hidden=true and hides the overlay but never restores focus to the Search trigger, leaving focus unrestored (Chromium blurs the now-hidden input, so focus reverts to the document body) and the next Tab restarts from the top of the page.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus is not contained within the search modal dialog when opened, allowing keyboard navigation to escape to background controls.
The resting focus order logically traverses the header controls, primary navigation links, and article body link in consistent top-to-bottom reading sequence.
Focus does not return to the 'Open search' button after the search dialog is dismissed.
No focus insertion barrier was found because activating the reveal control moves focus directly into the revealed content.

ruleName: SaaS analytics dashboard (Metrico) 'Dashboard settings' modal. On open, focus correctly moves into the dialog; on close (via ×, Cancel, Save, or Escape — all routed through one closeDialog()), focus is dropped to document.body instead of returning to the 'Dashboard settings' trigger, so the next Tab restarts at the top-of-page header nav.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus is not contained within the 'Dashboard settings' modal dialog, allowing keyboard navigation to leak to background elements behind the modal.
The resting focus order logically follows the visual and semantic structure of the page, moving through the top navigation links and then the main toolbar buttons.
Focus does not return to the Dashboard settings button after the settings dialog is dismissed.
No focus insertion barrier was found because activating the Dashboard settings control automatically moves keyboard focus directly into the revealed content.

ruleName: Real-estate listings results page: a toolbar 'Filters' button reveals a filter form (price/bedrooms/type) that is position:fixed to appear right beside the button on the left, but whose markup is the last element in the document after every listing and the footer; the toggle adds .open only, with no focus move, so the next Tab goes to 'Sort: Newest' and then through eight listing links before reaching the filter controls.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The resting tab sequence follows a logical, predictable reading and operation order from header navigation to filter controls, property listing cards row-by-row, and footer links.
Activating the Filters button reveals a filter form whose interactive controls are neither focused upon opening nor inserted immediately after the button in the tab order.

ruleName: Self-paced LMS course outline (ordered list of Start + Module 1-4). Links carry positive tabindex 1,5,4,3,2, so Tab visits Start then Module 4,3,2,1 - reversing the visible, content-meaningful study sequence the page explicitly says must be done in order. Canonical F44 reversed-list pattern in a real course page.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The keyboard focus order traverses the sequential course modules in reverse order (Start here, then Module 4, 3, 2, and 1), conflicting with the numbered sequence and explicit instructions to complete the modules in order.

ruleName: BOUNDARY PASS. Community-garden waitlist form with stacked Full name (valid), Email (value 'priya.nair@', invalid), Phone (valid). The error 'Email address is incomplete — add the part after the @.' is rendered inside the Email field's own block directly under the Email input, which carries the red invalid border. There is NO aria-describedby — identification rests entirely on presentation, done correctly.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The full name field is not in an error state and was not rejected, so there is no error identification to evaluate.
The error for the email address field is clearly identified and described in text.
The optional phone field is not in an error state and no error was triggered for it, so 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this element.

ruleName: Healthcare patient-portal blood-pressure intake. Side-by-side Systolic (value 118, normal) and Diastolic (value 135, out of range) number inputs. The error 'Diastolic must be between 40 and 120 mmHg.' is placed in the Systolic column under the Systolic input, and the Systolic input carries the red alert border; the out-of-range Diastolic has no message. No aria-describedby.

Recipe "cook mode" view (Hearthline — slow-braised short ribs). Each numbered step's coloured badge was made a single focusable static element (span.badge.focusable[tabindex="0"]) so a "mark this step done" coachmark could appear on focus, but the step's real "Start … timer" <button> is nested INSIDE that same focusable badge, so every timed step (3 of them) yields two consecutive tab stops for one control.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order sequentially moves through recipe steps 2, 3, and 4 before reaching the completion action, preserving the intended reading and operation order.
Focusable generic container elements wrap interactive buttons, creating redundant and confusing duplicate tab stops immediately before the controls they enclose.

ruleName: Restaurant ordering site: a top-bar 'Menu ▾' button reveals a navigation flyout (role=menu) that appears visually directly under the button but whose markup is the last element in <body>; the click handler flips .open and aria-expanded only, with no focus move, so the next Tab from the button goes to the first page link ('Start your order'), not the menu items.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The resting focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom reading and operational sequence through the header, main content sections, and footer.
Revealed menu content is not inserted immediately after its trigger in the focus order, nor is focus moved into it upon activation.

ruleName: Arabic RTL developer forum thread: each comment has a 'رد' (Reply) button; activating Reply on the first comment reveals a reply form whose markup is appended at the very end of the thread DOM (after every other post and the footer) by a framework rendering one shared form per thread; the toggle flips .open/aria-expanded only with no focus move, so the next Tab goes to 'إعجاب' (Like) and through the rest of the thread before reaching the textarea.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom and right-to-left sequence that preserves meaning and operation flow for this Arabic RTL layout.
Activating the reply button reveals a response form that neither receives focus automatically nor is placed immediately after the opener in the focus order.

ruleName: CONTROL / discrimination foil (PASS). Event-ticketing phone field, post-submit error state — near-identical component to case-01. The retained value is '(202) 555-CALL', which genuinely contains parentheses, a space, a dash, and the letters C-A-L-L. The field is digits-only and the visible associated error reads 'Phone number must contain only digits. rubricVerdicts.summary: The input error is clearly identified in text describing the specific format violation and is programmatically associated with the field.

ruleName: Developer issue tracker (Forge) label-chip list. Each chip's × opens an alertdialog confirm; confirming deletes the chip and moves focus to the NEXT chip's × (falling back to the previous chip when the deleted one was last, and to '+ Add label' when none remain). This is the F85 tag-delete exception that must NOT be flagged. Cancel returns to the chip's × (chip survives).

rubricVerdicts.summary: The resting keyboard focus order traverses the label removal buttons and the add label control in a logical top-to-bottom, left-to-right sequence that preserves meaning and operability.
Focus successfully returns to the opener button after the confirmation dialog is dismissed.
Revealed content receives programmatic focus upon activation of the opening control, satisfying focus insertion requirements.

ruleName: Job board / ATS profile (Hirelane) with an 'Edit profile' button opening a three-step modal wizard (Basics → Availability → Summary). Each step moves focus to its first field; the final step swaps Next for Done. Pressing Done commits the edited values, closes the wizard, and returns focus to the originating 'Edit profile' trigger — the same return as Cancel and Escape — the affirmative PASS for terminal-confirm dismissal.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The resting tab order follows a logical top-to-bottom and left-to-right progression through the navigation links to the main content action.
Focus successfully returns to the 'Edit profile' opener button after the revealed modal is dismissed.
Activating the Edit profile button moves focus directly into the revealed dialog, satisfying the focus insertion requirement.

ruleName: PASS counter-example: a nonprofit donation form laid out with CSS flexbox 'order' so the amount block sits visually on top while it is authored SECOND in the DOM. Positive tabindex 1-5 is used DELIBERATELY to restore the visually-meaningful entry order (amount -> custom -> name -> email -> Donate). Uses positive tabindex but PRESERVES meaning, so it must not be flagged.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom sequence through the donation amount options, user details, and submit button, preserving the form's meaning and operation.

ruleName: Pulsar Platform API reference (rate-limiting page): the abbreviation 'TBA' is expanded only inside a pure-CSS :hover bubble containing the load-bearing burst formula (2x rate for ~5s) stated nowhere else. rubricVerdicts.summary: The custom hover tooltip obscures surrounding text content and cannot be dismissed via the Escape key without moving the pointer.
The custom tooltip cannot be reached by the pointer because a 10px physical gap between the trigger and the tooltip causes the content to disappear upon moving the cursor toward it.
The tooltip content revealed on hover remains persistent while the trigger remains hovered, without auto-dismissing on a timer.

ruleName: Hotel booking review, post-submit error state. Check-in '2026-08-01', check-out '2026-09-25' (55 nights — check-out IS after check-in). ruleName: E-commerce checkout payment row (Card number / Expiry / CVV) in a flex row. rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was detected or demonstrated for the 'Your name' field, so 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this control.

The focus sequence systematically navigates the schedule grid column-by-column (each day from morning to afternoon) before reaching the submit button, preserving the logical meaning and operability of the task.

The focus order follows a systematic column-by-column traversal down each day of the availability schedule before reaching the submit button, preserving meaning and operability.

ruleName: Healthcare patient portal (Riverbend) medication list with per-row Remove and an alertdialog confirm. Cancel ('Keep it') correctly returns focus to the Remove trigger, but Confirm ('Remove') deletes the row, calls window.scrollTo(0,0), and focuses the first header nav link instead of the next/previous medication's controls — the logical neighbor F85 requires when the trigger is removed.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus escapes the open confirmation modal dialog and moves to background page elements during tabbing.
The resting tab order follows a logical sequence from the top navigation through each medication row in order.
Focus successfully returns to the opener control after the revealed confirmation dialog is dismissed.

ruleName: E-commerce seller console (Looma) orders table where every row has an identical Actions menu button (aria-haspopup/aria-expanded, role=menu/menuitem, accessible names, correct on-open focus). Three menus (rows 1,3,4) return focus to their trigger on close; the visually-identical twin on row 2 (#LG-90411) calls document.activeElement.blur() on close, dropping focus to document.body so the next Tab restarts from the sidebar nav. The page fails because of that one broken menu.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The resting focus order follows a logical and systematic sequence, navigating through the sidebar menu items before proceeding row-by-row through the main table action buttons.
Dismissing the second row's Actions menu drops focus onto the document body instead of returning it to the opener button.
Revealed menu content is properly managed upon activation without breaking the logical focus order.

ruleName: Bank reset-password screen redisplayed after rejecting a reused password; the field shows a red outline + a red CSS ::before key glyph and carries aria-invalid='true', but emits NO error text, aria-errormessage, or aria-describedby — nothing in words states what is wrong or why.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The rejected password field is flagged only with visual styling and aria-invalid without any textual description of the error.
No error was demonstrated or flagged for the 'Confirm new password' field.

ruleName: Healthcare new-patient intake, post-submit error state. Date-of-birth field retains '03/14/2027', which already conforms exactly to MM/DD/YYYY. The visible associated error reads 'Date of birth is invalid. Please use the MM/DD/YYYY format.' — naming a constraint that is already satisfied. The actual error (a birth date set in the future) is never described, so the only guidance is a no-op fix.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The target input 'Legal name' is valid and not in an error state, so error identification does not apply to it.
The error message misidentifies the problem by instructing the user to use the MM/DD/YYYY format when the retained value is already formatted as MM/DD/YYYY.

ruleName: Cedar Mutual Auto 3-step quote wizard silently advanced to 'Step 3 of 3, Review & buy' after an invalid ZIP ('0', too short) on Step 1 was swallowed — Step 2 (coverage options) was skipped because the rating engine had no usable ZIP. The review summary freezes the invalid ZIP '0' as read-only text and shows a placeholder premium '$—'; no error text appears. Cross-page silent-advance variant. LONG-TAIL; content-domain insurance quote wizard, APG stepper + dl review, lazy-validation persona.

Government benefits-enrollment form (Step 2 of 4) where every field has explicit positive tabindex 1-8, but a later-added required 'Daytime phone' field was dropped in with NO tabindex. Because positive-tabindex elements are visited first, the un-indexed phone field is tabbed dead last, after the Submit button. The F44 edit-drift variant the technique itself describes.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order skips the required Daytime Phone field and places it after the form submission buttons.

ruleName: Arabic-language (dir=rtl) clinic appointment form localized from an English template. In RTL the rightmost box is visually first (given name; day), but positive tabindex was numbered left-to-right (1,2,3...) for the original LTR layout and never updated. Tab thus visits family->father->given and year->month->day - the exact reverse of the right-to-left reading order.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order navigates the right-to-left form fields in reverse logical sequence, moving from Family Name to First Name and Year to Day.

ruleName: B2B wholesale coffee order grid: 3x3 matrix of quantity inputs (rows=pack sizes, columns=blends). Visual layout is row-major but Tab walks column-by-column (all sizes of one blend before the next), achieved purely by column-major DOM source order + CSS Grid placement (no tabindex). Completing one product's full size-ladder at a time is a logical purchasing workflow.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The keyboard focus order systematically traverses the matrix column by column (all pack sizes for each coffee blend in turn) before reaching the submit button, preserving the logical meaning and operability of the form.

ruleName: Mortgage 'configure & compare rate locks' tool with two side-by-side columns (Plan A 30-yr, Plan B 15-yr), each stacking Loan amount / Down payment / Points. Positive tabindex row-interleaves the columns (A.amt=1,B.amt=2,A.down=3,B.down=4,A.pts=5,B.pts=6), so Tab ping-pongs left-right across the gutter, breaking each plan's must-be-completed-as-a-unit field group.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus ping-pongs between the Plan A and Plan B form sections across rows rather than completing each plan's inputs sequentially, disrupting the logical task flow.

ruleName: SaaS 'set your password' screen, post-submit error state. Password field holds a 12-character value (shown as 12 bullets); the visible associated error reads 'Password must be at least 8 characters.' The page's own requirements checklist marks 'At least 8 characters' as MET (green) and 'At least one number' as the only UNMET rule (red). The error asserts a length rule already passed; the actual unmet rule (digit) triggered rejection but is not the one described, so the error contradicts the page's own checklist.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message misidentifies the failure by stating that the password must be at least 8 characters when the entered password already meets the length requirement and fails the number requirement instead.

ruleName: Government SNAP-benefits two-column grid form. Row 1 has First name (left, filled 'Maria') and Last name (right, filled). After a failed submit the error 'First name is required.' is placed in the right-column cell directly under the Last name input, and Last name (not First name) gets aria-invalid=true. No aria-describedby links the message to any control.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message is displayed under and flags the wrong form field, failing to properly identify the error for the input.
The error message displayed under the 'Last (family) name' field misidentifies the error as 'First name is required.'
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the Middle initial field.
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the optional Preferred name field.

ruleName: PASS boundary (hardest 'tedious vs impedes operation' line): a developer API reference sidebar where each category section header (Getting started / Core / Advanced) is a focusable static span[tabindex=0], adding an extra Tab stop per category. The stops are merely tedious — each label heads its OWN group, no link is duplicated, and no stop is wedged between two coupled controls.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom sequence through the navigation sidebar followed by the main content action.
The focusable section labels in the navigation sidebar introduce groups of links without duplicating controls or interrupting coupled form sequences.

ruleName: Municipal government portal: a 'Subscribe to alerts' button in a top announcement bar reveals a centered non-modal newsletter dialog whose markup is the last block before </body>; the open handler only toggles a CSS .open class and never moves focus, so after keyboard activation focus stays on the trigger and the next Tab lands on the first nav/content link, not the dialog.

Focus does not return to the opening trigger button when the modal dialog is dismissed.

ruleName: University admissions page: the 'Explore Northgate ▾' mega-menu button is in the header partial, but the mega-menu panel is emitted by the footer theme partial, so its markup sits near the end of the DOM while position:absolute;top:96px floats it up under the header to look attached; opening it only toggles .open/aria-expanded with no focus move, so the next Tab from the trigger goes to header/main-content links, not into the menu.

ruleName: Lakeview Dental month-grid date picker for September 2026: a 7-column calendar of real day <button>s placed by CSS grid-column/grid-row, rendering dates that ascend in normal reading order. The buttons are emitted COLUMN-MAJOR in the DOM (all Mondays, then all Tuesdays...). No tabindex, no JS. ruleName: Homeware ecommerce checkout (en-GB); shipping postcode 9021 is too short and billing postcode SW1A 0AA! has an illegal character, but both reuse one SVG sprite and both <svg role=img> wrappers carry the identical hardcoded aria-label="Invalid input".

ruleName: Boundary PASS counter-example: a coffee-roaster wholesale page where the 'Get the wholesale price list' button reveals a non-modal dialog whose markup is placed immediately after the trigger, so the dialog's email field is the very next node in source order; the visibility-only toggle is correct here and dismissal returns focus to the trigger.

ruleName: HR 360-degree competency review: a 4x4 matrix where each cell is its own <input type=range> slider (rows=competencies, columns=rater perspectives Self/Manager/Peer/Direct report).
